clue.text: It may force people into early retirement

definitions.text: It may force people into early retirement

parts.words: It may force people into early retirement
parts.note: retirement here is going indoors for the night, not leaving work: an order that sends everyone home early

explanation.surface: A policy that pushes workers to give up their jobs young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests pensions; it is retiring indoors, as a town's evening order to stay off the streets compels.
explanation.definitionFit: An order keeping people off the streets after a set hour makes them withdraw indoors early.

clue.text: An abandoned lot, shipwrecked mariners?

definitions.meaning: a group of people thrown out or discarded

explanation.surface: A deserted plot of land, or sailors after a wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: People cast off or rejected, and sailors stranded on an island after wreckage.

clue.text: Diet for instance ingested by indisposed miner

indicators.note: ingested means swallowed, so the example abbreviation goes inside the scrambled word
indisposed means unwell, out of sorts, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: A sick miner swallows his diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indisposed' (unwell, out of order) gives RIMEN; 'ingested by' means swallowed, so the example abbreviation goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed course of eating and exercise, a regimen, is a diet plan.

clue.text: Result of being carried on a stretcher?

definitions.text: Result of being carried on a stretcher?

parts.words: Result of being carried on a stretcher?
parts.note: not a medical stretcher but a torture rack, which pulls the body longer

explanation.surface: What happens to a patient taken on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'stretcher' suggests a patient; read it as something that stretches, like a rack.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stretched produces lengthening.

clue.text: What. Jack Point had to do at this concert?'

definitions.text: What. Jack Point had to do
definitions.meaning: Jack Point is the jester in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Yeomen of the Guard, whose number begins 'I have a song to sing, O'
an informal gathering where everyone joins in the music

explanation.surface: A quiz question about a Gilbert and Sullivan jester's duties at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: The jester's task was to perform a tune; a communal sing-along is also called by this name.

clue.text: Unfair description of sickness benefits

parts.note: a phrase meaning profits obtained dishonestly, read literally as payments obtained through illness

explanation.surface: Calling sick pay unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'ill' plus 'gotten' describes money got by being sick.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means dishonestly acquired profits, and literally sickness-acquired benefits.

clue.text: One of the bloods of Kensington?

definitions.text: One of the bloods of Kensington?

parts.words: One of the bloods of Kensington?
parts.note: Kensington's road beside Hyde Park shares its name with theatrical fake blood, and bloods also means young dandies

explanation.surface: A young aristocratic dandy from a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloods' suggests fashionable young men; Kensington Gore is a London street and stage slang for fake blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilt blood, and the second word of Kensington Gore, the London road.

clue.text: Gushing advice to avoid friction

explanation.surface: Effusive tips on keeping the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilled source of petroleum, and an instruction to lubricate generously.

clue.text: See 5
For whom one alone waited at 'the gate

definitions.text: For whom one alone waited at 'the gate

parts.words: For whom one alone waited at
parts.note: Tennyson's poem has the lover call 'Come into the garden' to this girl, being 'here at the gate alone'

explanation.surface: A person waited alone by the gate for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's line: 'Come into the garden, Maud, ... I am here at the gate alone'.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl addressed in Tennyson's poem, awaited by the speaker.

clue.text: So. a ring can give her married status

indicators.note: the clue words can be rearranged to give something new, signalling a mix of their letters

explanation.surface: A wedding ring confers on a woman the standing of a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can give' tells you to rearrange SO A RING.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title for a married woman, equivalent to Mrs, names her status as a wife.

clue.text: -Rock singer

definitions.meaning: a cliff on the Rhine bearing this name
the siren of German legend who sang from that cliff and lured boatmen to their deaths

explanation.surface: A rock musician.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine cliff and the legendary siren who sat on it singing share the same name.

clue.text: Gore and mad turmoil of battle

indicators.note: turmoil is wild disorder, so the letters of the words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Bloodshed and frenzied chaos of warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turmoil of' scrambles GORE AND MAD, all ten letters including AND.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical site of the final conflict between good and evil, now any catastrophic clash.

clue.text: Antelopes said 'to show such, intelligence

indicators.note: said tells you the word is spoken rather than written, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: gnus, or wildebeest, are African antelopes

explanation.surface: Clever antelopes demonstrating their smarts.
explanation.walkthrough: GNUS spoken (the G is silent) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the sense of information or reports received.

clue.text: A.celebrity's due

parts.note: a lion is a celebrated person, and a lion's portion is the biggest part

explanation.surface: What a famous person deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lion' is a socially celebrated person, so the celebrity's portion is the largest share.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest portion, read as what a famous person is owed.

clue.text: She can adopt ten neat disguises.

indicators.note: disguises change how something looks, so the letters are put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman who can take on various neat costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguises' rearranges TEN NEAT into a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so it can stand for any woman.

clue.text: An alarm clock ?. What a surprise'!

definitions.meaning: something that makes you open your sight in the morning

explanation.surface: An alarm goes off, astonishingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation that startles, and, literally, a device that wakes you.

clue.text: Toys with sweets

definitions.meaning: custard-and-sponge desserts, or puddings in general

explanation.surface: Playthings that come with candy.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle is to dally; trifles are also layered custard desserts.

clue.text: That of, one by Tosti was valedictory

definitions.text: That of, one by Tosti was valedictory

parts.words: That of, one by Tosti was valedictory
parts.note: Paolo Tosti wrote the famous ballad 'Good-bye', whose name is itself a farewell

explanation.surface: A farewell piece by the composer Tosti.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosti, an Italian composer, wrote 'Good-bye': the name of that piece is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a piece of music, here a farewell.

clue.text: A person of no 'distinction ?

parts.note: an unspecified individual, with no particular identity, though the phrase 'a ...' also means somebody important

explanation.surface: A nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means an unidentified individual, yet 'to be a ...' means to be important: hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun refers to an unnamed, undistinguished individual.

clue.text: Unspeakably small ?

parts.note: split as small (mini) and silent (mum), it reads as a tiny quiet thing

explanation.surface: Indescribably tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it: MINI is small, MUM means silent, so 'unspeakably small'.
explanation.definitionFit: The least possible amount, extremely small.

clue.text: A number continue to find fault with the figure

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
to keep on carping at someone is to nag on

explanation.surface: Someone keeps criticising a particular number shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric shape with nine sides.

clue.text: Does he complain of bad shooting?

definitions.text: Does he complain of bad shooting?

parts.words: Does he complain of bad shooting?
parts.note: a grumbler, but literally someone shooting the game bird of the moors

explanation.surface: A man moaning about poor marksmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: A complainer; also read as a hunter of grouse, so poor shooting fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumbler or complainer.

clue.text: Lear character could stand in for Rudolf the Reindeer

definitions.text: Lear character could stand in for Rudolf the Reindeer

parts.words: Lear character could stand in for Rudolf the Reindeer
parts.note: Edward Lear's nonsense poem features a creature with a luminous nose, who could replace the red-nosed reindeer

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean figure deputising for Santa's reindeer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests Shakespeare's king; it is Edward Lear, the nonsense poet, whose 'The Dong with a Luminous Nose' has a glowing nose like Rudolph's.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Lear creature and the reindeer are famed for a nose that lights up.

clue.text: Not where ships undergo their trials

definitions.text: Not where ships undergo their trials

parts.words: Not where ships undergo their trials
parts.note: ships berth in these basins, but the trials held in them, as in a courtroom enclosure, are for people, not ships

explanation.surface: A place where ships do not do their sea trials.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom 'dock' is where the accused stand trial; the shipyard docks see no such trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtroom enclosures for defendants share a name with harbour basins for ships.

clue.text: One inimical to game, and wine?

definitions.text: One inimical to game, and wine?

parts.words: One inimical to game, and wine?
parts.note: someone who ruins the fun of a game, and, split in two, someone who ruins the fortified Portuguese wine

explanation.surface: An enemy of both hunting and drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' means sport, so a ruiner of fun; split after five letters, the word also ruins port, the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy who ruins others' enjoyment.

clue.text: Letter from Greece-the 20 one:

definitions.meaning: the ninth character of the Greek alphabet
20-down is MINIMUM; this word means a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A letter posted from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek vowel, and a very small quantity.

clue.text: Bird in the wilderness

indicators.note: in shows the bird sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is a kind of sea eagle, a large coastal raptor, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Clannish form of romance

indicators.note: a form of a word is a version of it reshaped, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A clan-based variety of love story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges ROMANCE into a Scottish clan name; 'Clannish' means belonging to a clan.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland Scottish clan, so the name is one belonging to a clan.

clue.text: Passage round the poles is characteristic

indicators.note: round means the characteristic word goes around the poles, enclosing them

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic
N and S, the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A voyage around the poles is typical.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'round' as the trait wrapped round N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing or travelling through.

clue.text: Blake's tiger's was fearful

parts.note: William Blake's poem The Tyger asks what hand could frame the beast's 'fearful' balance of form

explanation.surface: The poet's tiger was frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fearful' looks like a description of the tiger; it completes Blake's line 'Could frame thy fearful ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted phrase from the poem is completed by this word for balanced proportion.

clue.text: England as one German described it

definitions.text: England as one German described it

parts.words: England as one German described it
parts.note: Edward German, the English composer, wrote the comic opera titled after a jolly, old-fashioned England

explanation.surface: A German person's description of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' looks like a nationality; it is the composer Edward German, whose 1902 operetta is Merrie England.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic spelling of jolly in the operetta's title, describing a cheerful England.
